rationale: One randomized open-label dysmenorrhea trial (n=80) reports lower three-month menstrual weakness scores with fennel soft capsules versus no medication (6.65 to 2.88 vs 6.39 flat, p=.001; abstract prints a conflicting control value; PMID25085020). Two other dysmenorrhea trials were inconclusive for fatigue (essential oil overall p=.08 with differential discontinuation; 2007 extract p=.058 without reported direction), and crushed-seed infusion and honey-mixture surveys lack controlled fatigue data. Unblinded design, reporting conflict, null comparators, and non-Parkinson menstrual weakness keep the lean against worsening at minimal_signal. A separate 2019 extract trial records fatigue in 8 of 36 participants in each arm after treatment. It measures occurrence and has unresolved comparator and tabular details. It supplies no evidence for a contrary directional result on the frozen endpoint.
